articles.headline: Timberwolves' Anthony Edwards (knee) to miss up to 2 months, sources say
articles.description: Timberwolves star Anthony Edwards will undergo an arthroscopic procedure on his ailing right knee Thursday that will sideline him up to two months, sources told ESPN's Shams Charania.
articles.headlineJa: ティンバーウルブズのアンソニー・エドワーズ（膝）が最大2カ月欠場へ、関係者が明らかに
articles.descriptionJa: ティンバーウルブズのスター、アンソニー・エドワーズは木曜日に右膝の関節鏡手術を受ける予定で、これにより最大2カ月間戦列を離脱することになると、ESPNのシャムス・チャラニア氏が関係者から報じた。
articles.body:
Minnesota Timberwolves star Anthony Edwards will undergo an arthroscopic procedure on his ailing right knee that will sideline him for up to two months, sources told ESPN's Shams Charania.

Edwards has been on the injury report with the injury, the same leg he dealt with runner's knee last season. 

Edwards most recently scored 47 points in Minnesota's overtime loss at Cleveland on Monday. It was the seventh time in Edwards' five-year career he had at least 47 points in a game.

The Timberwolves are off to a 3-1 start and host the Golden State Warriors on Wednesday night.

articles.description: The NBA is back. The buzz never left. Bookmark this page for the latest news, rumblings and analysis from ESPN's insiders.

articles.body:
The NBA is only a few games deep, but leaguewide buzz never stops. 

The LeBron James and Jaylen Brown era with the Philadelphia 76ers got off to an ideal start by spoiling ring night for the New York Knicks. The Detroit Pistons also returned to their regular-season dominance with a win over the Boston Celtics, and the Oklahoma City Thunder struck the first rivalry blow against the San Antonio Spurs this season.

Now, what will Giannis Antetokounmpo's first season away from Milwaukee look like? And how will the other new faces in new places make their impact this season?

All season, bookmark this page for the latest news and reactions from our ESPN NBA insiders.

Quick links:

Free agency grades | Trade grades

Trade tracker | Transactions | Offseason buzz

Depth charts | Trade machine | More

Oct. 27

What Edwards' injury means for Wolves

 

On Monday, Anthony Edwards looked like an MVP candidate as he poured in 47 points in Cleveland. On Tuesday, that dream was dashed early, as ESPN's Shams Charania reported that Edwards will miss up to two months due to right knee surgery.

Minnesota can still contend this season, as long as Edwards returns healthy at the end of that projected time frame. The partnership of Edwards and LaMelo Ball was one of the most exciting elements of the new season, and the Timberwolves raced to a 3-1 start featuring three blowout wins, with an overtime loss to the Cavaliers marring their ledger. At the end of two more months, 52 games will remain on their schedule.

But they won't be comfortable in the meantime. The Timberwolves have a relatively shallow roster, and their bench will be stretched thin once sixth man Ayo Dosunmu moves into the starting lineup to replace Edwards. Their two-way star's absence also reduces any margin for error with the rest of the roster; Ball is notoriously injury-prone, and if both guards are ever out at the same time, a lengthy losing streak could ensue.

 Edwards to undergo surgery, miss up to two months

Minnesota Timberwolves star Anthony Edwards will undergo an arthroscopic procedure on his ailing right knee that will sideline him for up to two months, sources told ESPN's Shams Charania.

Edwards has been on the injury report for the injury. He dealt with runner's knee in the same leg last season.

Leonard out multiple weeks, misses return to LA

Toronto Raptors forward Kawhi Leonard will miss multiple weeks due to left knee swelling, sources told ESPN's Shams Charania. An MRI showed no structural damage, but the recovery will keep Leonard out of a return game at the LA Clippers on Nov. 2.

articles.headline: Ayesha Curry to star in holiday rom-com 'Second Chance Holiday,' premiering on Roku
articles.description: The wife of Stephen Curry will make her debut in a feature film leading role with Roku's "Second Chance Holiday."
articles.headlineJa: アイシャ・カリー、Rokuで配信のホリデー・ロマンティックコメディ『Second Chance Holiday』に主演
articles.descriptionJa: ステフィン・カリーの妻であるアイシャ・カリーが、Rokuの『Second Chance Holiday』で長編映画の主演デビューを果たす。
articles.body:
Ayesha Curry is set to star in Roku's holiday rom-com, "Second Chance Holiday," premiering Nov. 5, Roku announced Tuesday. It marks Curry's debut in a feature film leading role.

Roku shared the news with a trailer that was released on social media. The channel first announced the movie in July with Curry, the wife of Golden State Warriors star Stephen, as the headliner. However, the trailer and release date weren't made available until Tuesday.

Ayesha will be starring alongside Matthew Daddario, the brother of movie star Alexandra.

"It's an honor to be part of Second Chance Holiday alongside such a talented cast and crew," Curry said in a July statement. "There's something truly magical about holiday rom-coms. They invite you into these charming, cozy worlds where anything feels possible. Chelsey is such a fun, heartfelt character that I fell in love with while bringing her to life. I hope audiences fall in love with her too and enjoy Second Chance Holiday this holiday season."

The film follows Curry as a dating expert looking to break a "curse" of frequently getting dumped during the holiday season, according to Roku. She is reunited with her high school crush, played by Daddario, and wonders if the bad luck is the universe's way of pushing her back to her first love.

Stephen and Ayesha have been married for 15 years and share four children together. The four-time NBA champion responded to the trailer on X, calling Ayesha his "leading lady."

Though Ayesha has never secured a leading film role, she has experience in front of the camera.

Her most recent role was in the animation movie "GOAT," which was produced by her husband, who also appeared in the movie. Ayesha has been credited for appearances in Disney's "Hannah Montana" and "Good Luck Charlie," plus HBO's "Ballers."

Now, she'll make her debut in a film set for the holidays that will stream on Roku.

articles.headlineJa: 関係者談：ニックスのアシスタントコーチ、クリス・ジェントが私的事情により離脱
articles.descriptionJa: ニューヨーク・ニックスのアシスタントコーチ、クリス・ジェントが、個人的な理由により一定期間チームを離れることが、関係者へのESPNの取材で明らかになった。
articles.body:
NEW YORK -- New York Knicks assistant coach Chris Jent will be away from the team for an undisclosed amount of time due to personal reasons, sources confirmed to ESPN on Tuesday.

The Athletic was first to report the news.

Jent, 56, was a member of Mike Brown's staff in Cleveland and was on the Charlotte Hornets' coaching staff in 2024-25.

Jent was an interim coach with the Orlando Magic for 18 games in 2004-05. Jent played at Ohio State from 1988 to 1992.

articles.headline: NFL trade deadline grades: DeForest Buckner, Quenton Nelson dealt by Colts, more
articles.description: Does Buckner make the 49ers Super Bowl hopefuls? Will Quenton Nelson upgrade the Seahawks' O-line? We're grading NFL trades ahead of November's deadline.
articles.headlineJa: NFLトレード期限の評価：コルツがデフォレスト・バックナーやクエンティン・ネルソンを放出、ほか
articles.descriptionJa: バックナーは49ersをスーパーボウルへ導けるか？クエンティン・ネルソンはシーホークスのOL陣を強化できるか？11月の期限を前に、NFLのトレードを格付けする。
articles.body:
NFL analysts Ben Solak and Seth Walder are grading deals ahead of the 2026 trade deadline, which is Nov. 10 at 4 p.m. ET.

When grading trades, we evaluate them for each team based on on-field impact, cap implications, draft compensation and effects within the context of a team's overall short- and long-term outlooks. How confident are we in knowing if this is a good or bad decision? And how big is the impact of this decision? Both questions play a role in our grades, though a low-impact decision can still receive a strong or poor grade. Even with lower stakes, clear-cut wins or losses still matter.

Here are our evaluations for the first six deals of trading season, including the Colts sending guard Quenton Nelson to Seattle and defensive tackle DeForest Buckner to San Francisco. Check back through the deadline for grades on the biggest moves.

Jump to a trade:

Buckner | Nelson | Harrison 

Jurgens | Porter | McCarthy

Colts trade DT Buckner to 49ers

49ers get: DT DeForest Buckner

Colts get: 2027 fourth-round pick

49ers grade: A-

Colts grade: B-

As soon as the Colts emerged as a team who might engage in a trade-deadline teardown, it wasn't hard to see the dots connecting Buckner back to the 49ers. That became a reality Tuesday.

Even at age 32, Buckner can help the 49ers get after the quarterback, though his numbers have dipped this season. He has four sacks this season, but his pass rush win rate ranked in the 45th percentile among defensive tackles, alongside a 69th percentile pressure rate. That is a drop from last season. when he was in the 90th and 88th percentile in those metrics, respectively. However, that 2025 performance is a positive sign for what he could bring to the 49ers the rest of this season.

Extra pass-rushing help will be welcome in San Francisco, which ranks 19th in pass rush win rate. The 49ers have been without Nick Bosa, who has been out with a calf injury since Week 3 but is expected to return soon. Their pass defense is the only one of their major units (run and pass on offense and defense) that ranks outside the top seven in EPA per play (13th).

I'll admit I'm a little surprised the 49ers made this move considering they already have Osa Odighizuwa as a pass rush-first defensive tackle. But he can play next to Buckner -- especially on passing downs. Also, San Francisco's rash of defensive line injuries makes any help welcome.

This type of roster-bolstering move makes sense for San Francisco. The 49ers are the Super Bowl favorites, according to ESPN's Football Power Index. In fact, they are the favorites by a lot, with FPI giving them a 23% chance to win the Super Bowl (every other team is below 11%). Adding a player like Buckner to reinforce those chances is worthwhile.

articles.headline: Buckner, Nelson trades signal Colts' rebuild underway
articles.description: DeForest Buckner and Quenton Nelson are headed to contending teams. Could Jonathan Taylor be next?
articles.body:
INDIANAPOLIS -- DeForest Buckner had seen enough.

As the curtains closed Sunday on the Indianapolis Colts' third straight loss, punctuating a season that began with high hopes and devolved into a road to nowhere, the veteran defensive tackle finally let his emotions show.

Asked by a reporter how he felt after losing to the Minnesota Vikings to fall to 2-5, the three-time Pro Bowl selection was blunt.

"I don't know, how 'bout you guess," he said. "I'm frustrated. Same thing. We lost."

The losing wore on Buckner. But he and fellow Colts standout Quenton Nelson, an All-Pro guard, will no longer have to endure the frustration. Both were traded Tuesday during one of the most consequential days for the franchise since the stunning 2019 retirement of quarterback Andrew Luck.

But this development was much easier to predict than Luck's departure as it follows the firing of general manager Chris Ballard last week.

Assistant general manager Ed Dodds engineered Tuesday's deals, presumably at the direction of owner Carlie Irsay-Gordon. Buckner is heading back to the San Francisco 49ers, the team that drafted him and traded him to Indianapolis in 2020. Nelson is headed to the Seattle Seahawks, one of the Niners' main NFC West rivals. Both players were in the final year of their contracts and their futures in Indianapolis were uncertain at best.

Moves such as these appeared likely following Ballard's dismissal in his 10th season on the job. Ballard and the Colts had tried tweaking the roster to varying degrees in recent years. And they have tried every iteration of quarterback acquisition in their efforts to replace Luck.

In the end, it all amounted to nothing.

The Colts have not won the AFC South since 2014. They last made the playoffs in 2020. Their last postseason victory came in 2018. They've averaged 7.6 wins over the past five seasons. Even great players such as Buckner and Nelson weren't enough to overcome the club's other shortcomings.

Tuesday's difficult decisions made it official: The Colts are done with that chapter.

The next phase of franchise history will be a full rebuild. The Colts must embark on that rebuild without a first-round pick in 2027 as that selection is heading to the New York Jets to complete last year's Sauce Gardner trade. So, Tuesday's moves were a step toward rebuilding the draft capital that the team's next top executive will need to begin what will be a difficult job.

The Colts are expected to entertain additional deals with players such as running back Jonathan Taylor, nose tackle Grover Stewart and receiver Josh Downs attracting interest from other clubs.

But for now, Indianapolis has a single second-round pick in 2027, two third-round choices and two fourth-round selections among its selections. The Nelson deal garnered a 2027 third-round choice (along with a 2028 fifth-rounder) from Seattle, and Buckner netted a 2027 fourth-round choice from San Francisco.

articles.headline: Matt LaFleur isn't ruling out imminent practice return for Micah Parsons
articles.description: Green Bay Packers edge rusher Micah Parsons might finally be back on the practice field next week, more than 10 months after he underwent surgery on his left knee.
articles.body:
GREEN BAY, Wis. -- Green Bay Packers edge rusher Micah Parsons might finally be back on the practice field next week, more than 10 months after he underwent surgery on his left knee.

While nothing was definitive, coach Matt LaFleur on Tuesday changed the way he answered the weekly question about Parson's return to practice that he has gotten over the past month and a half.

"I sure hope so," LaFleur said.

Previously, the answer had always been a quick and hard no.

LaFleur acknowledged that his answer this time was different.

"It is," he said. "At the end of the day, that's the medical [decision]. Yeah, I'm itching [for] it, though, for sure."

LaFleur added: "I'm saying there's a chance."

Parsons tore the ACL and meniscus in his left knee on Dec. 14 and had surgery two weeks later. He remains on the physically unable to perform list. Once players on PUP return to practice, they have three weeks before they must be either added to the roster or placed on injured reserve.

Even if Parsons practices next week, it would be highly unlikely he could play in the Week 9 game at the Patriots.

It would not have made sense for the Packers to open Parsons' practice window this week because with a Thursday game against the Panthers coming up, they will not hold any regular practices this week. After visiting New England on Nov. 8, the Packers play at home against the Vikings in Week 10 and then have their bye in Week 11, so it's possible the Packers will hold Parsons out of game action until the first post-bye game on Nov. 25 at the Rams.

articles.headline: Is Fleetwood Town's defeat of Arsenal the biggest upset in League Cup history?
articles.description: Arsenal aren't the only Premier League side to suffer Cup humiliation; ESPN takes a look at all the famous "giant killings" in England's League Cup.
articles.body:
(Editor's note: This article was originally published in 2025 and has been updated following Fleetwood Town's triumph on Tuesday.)

A case can be made that Fleetwood Town's shock penalty shootout win over Arsenal is the biggest upset in League Cup history.

There have been plenty of remarkable boilovers through the years, so it's got competition, but the Gunners entered Tuesday evening's contest as the reigning Premier League champions and with just one loss across 11 league and UEFA Champions League fixtures this season.

Mikel Arteta's side fell behind in the 21st minute when Aaron Loupalo-Bi shook off the attention of Marli Salmon and fired an effort through the legs of keeper Illan Meslier. And while Viktor Gyökeres would pull the visitors back level five minutes into the second stanza and they would dominate possession, the Premier League giants couldn't find a winner inside 90 minutes - forcing the game to penalties.

- Hunter: If the Clásico is any indication, Mou's Madrid might be special again

- Ranked: Every Premier League team's money-per-points (after City cheated)

- Jones: Vozinha's Ballon d'Or night a perfect moment for soccer's dreamers

Both sides were perfect from the spot until Bruno Guimarães -- just months on from missing a penalty that would have put Brazil 1-0 up in their eventual round of 16 loss to Norway at the FIFA World Cup -- was denied by Fleetwood custodian Jay Lynch.

Teenage defender Conor Haughey then smashed home the winning penalty to spark a pitch invasion as the Cod Army knocked off a side 84 places above them in the English pyramid and claimed possibly the greatest win in their history.

"We talked about Grimsby beating Man United last year; we compared it, even though these are the champions, and thought, if we gave it a go, let's see what happens," Lynch told Sky. "It's amazing for the club, for the club, it means everything to everyone."

It was an evening tinged by a level of madness of all sorts: 16-year-old Max Dowman sent off in the 85th minute after lashing out following a physical challenge from Harrison Neal and play suspended for eight minutes after a drone was flown above the pitch in just the second minute.

"I'm gonna be honest, we haven't practiced once, in terms of penalties," Fleetwood boss Matt Lawlor told Sky. "I'm not gonna sit here and blag you and say we've done some meticulous penalties; we haven't practiced."

It's a result that slots comfortably into ESPN's stockpile of giant killings in the League Cup.

Manchester United hit new depths when they were bundled out of the second round of the League Cup by League Two outfit Grimsby Town in 2025 -- their first ever cup elimination from a side in England's fourth tier.

articles.headline: Espanyol, with Watt among owners, sack González after loss to 4th-tier side
articles.description: Espanyol, the LaLiga side whose ownership group includes former NFL star J.J. Watt, have sacked coach Manolo González following Tuesday's Copa del Rey exit to fourth-tier side Sestao River.
articles.body:
Espanyol, the LaLiga side whose ownership group includes former NFL star J.J. Watt, have sacked coach Manolo González following Tuesday's Copa del Rey exit to fourth-tier side Sestao River.

Sestao scored twice in extra time, including a dramatic 121st-minute winner, to seal a shock 4-3 victory and knock the Primera División side out in the first round.

González, 47, was already under pressure following Sunday's 2-1 defeat to newly promoted Racing Santander.

That loss left Barcelona-based Espanyol in the relegation zone in LaLiga and extended their winless run to five league games. They have won just twice in all competitions this season.

Defeat to lower-league opposition proved the final straw for the club's owners, Velocity Sports Limited (VSL), the investment group led by American businessman Alan Pace and backed by investors including Watt.

González becomes the second coach to be dismissed by VSL in four days after Burnley, the English Championship club also owned by the group, sacked Nicky Hayen.

Burnley, who were relegated from the Premier League last season, have won just one of their opening 12 Championship fixtures.

A 4-1 defeat at Lincoln City on Saturday preceded Hayen's dismissal, with González following him out of the door on Tuesday.

VSL acquired Burnley in 2020, overseeing three relegations from the Premier League and two promotions from the Championship.

The group took control of Espanyol in October 2025, replacing Chinese company Rastar Group as the Catalan club's majority shareholder.

Watt, who played as a defensive end for the Houston Texans and Arizona Cardinals, has become a high-profile figure in the ownership group, attending games, supporting the clubs on social media and wearing their merchandise during appearances on American television.

articles.headline: Montez Sweat returns to Bears following 'devastating' 2-game suspension
articles.description: Bears DE Montez Sweat is back with the team following his "devastating" two-game suspension violating the NFL's performance enhancing substances policy.
articles.body:
LAKE FOREST, Ill. -- Chicago Bears defensive end Montez Sweat said Tuesday that he unintentionally took a banned substance that led to a two-game suspension for violating the NFL's performance enhancing substances policy.

"It definitely was accidental," Sweat said. "It was a surprise. But you take a lick on the chin and keep moving forward."

Sweat, 30, was sidelined for back-to-back wins over the Falcons and Patriots. He was reinstated Oct. 23, one day after Chicago beat New England, and will return to action in Week 8 when the Bears play the Seahawks on "Monday Night Football."

The defensive end said it was "devastating" to be away from his team and see the consequences the suspension will have on his reputation.

"It's definitely something I've got to live with for my career," he said. "I never want to cheat the game, and I would never do it intentionally, but what happened, happened and I'm moving forward."

Sweat declined to give specifics about what led to his failed test or when he tested positive while clarifying that there was no wrongdoing by the Bears nutritional or training staff. He said he did not consider appealing the suspension and took "full responsibility" for his actions, though he did not commit to making any specific changes to his regimen to prevent a future positive test.

"I've been in the league going on Year 8 now," he said. "I haven't wound up with a positive like that before, so I guess I'll just get back to my regular routine now."

Sweat is Chicago's highest-paid defensive player after he signed a four-year, $98 million deal ($24.5 million annually) upon being traded to the Bears in 2023. He had a career-high 12.5 sacks that season between his time in Washington and Chicago and recorded his second season of double-digit sacks (10) in 2025.

Coach Ben Johnson characterized Sweat's 2025 campaign as the edge rusher's best season as pro and noted that he believed the defensive end "affecting the quarterback a different type of way." Sweat said it was "tough" to face Johnson after learning of his suspension.

"Nobody wants to go look someone in the eye after you've done something detrimental like that to the team, but those are things you have to do to move forward," Sweat said.

The former first-round pick ranks fourth on the team with two sacks and has seven tackles including two tackles for loss. His suspension also came with a significant financial punishment. Sweat forfeited $2.3 million of his 2026 base salary for missing two games, while the guarantees on the remaining $12.7 million he's owed this season and all future years ($21 million in 2027) have been voided.

"I take everything that comes with it," Sweat said. "The only thing I can do now is just look forward and continue to play."

articles.headline: Yamal excited despite Ballon d'Or miss: 'Good things take time'
articles.description: Barcelona star Lamine Yamal won best young talent for a third-straight year at Monday's Ballon d'Or, but the 19-year-old has his sights set on the big prize.
articles.body:
Spain and Barcelona star Lamine Yamal was voted best young talent for a third-straight year at Monday's Ballon d'Or award ceremony, but the 19-year-old winger clearly has his sights set on the big prize won by Harry Kane.

Yamal, 19, finished third in the voting behind Bayern Munich and England star Kane and Real Madrid's Kylian Mbappé, who finished second.

The World Cup winner took to social media Tuesday night to reassure fans that missing out on soccer's top individual prize wouldn't get his spirts down.

"IT WILL COME, good things take time, I trust in the path I'm building," Yamal wrote. "No rush, just excitement and the calm assurance that one day my time will come.

"Congratulations to the winners. My focus is back on what matters most: making FC Barcelona win again."

The Barcelona teenager was among the leading contenders to win the award after a strong 2025-26 campaign, with 25 goals and 20 assists in 57 appearances to help Barcelona defend their LaLiga title and win the Spanish Supercopa.

He was also a key contributor to the Spain side that won the 2026 World Cup, despite Yamal scoring only one goal as he returned to the play in the summer following an injury late in the club season with Barcelona.

Yamal started seven of the Spain's eight games and was a constant menace down the right wing while attracting double teams throughout the tournament in North America, where La Roja won their second World Cup.

His Spain manager Luis de la Fuente, who won the Ballon d'Or for men's coach of the year, said after the ceremony on Monday: "Lamine Yamal is going to win many Ballon d'Or awards, many individual trophies, but more importantly, he is going to win many more team trophies. I know he values that more."

A 2024 European Champion, Yamal, 19, has already won three LaLiga titles with Barça.

Yamal won the Kopa Trophy, handed to the best young player in the world under the age of 21, ahead of his Spain and Barcelona teammate Pau Cubarsí.

Barcelona sit atop LaLiga after a stellar start to the season saw them win their first eight games, with Yamal scoring eight goals and adding six assists along the way.

Information from The Associated Press was used in this report.

articles.headline: Ballon d'or winner Harry Kane gets hero's welcome on Bayern Munich return
articles.description: After an historic Ballon d'Or win and an emotional speech, Harry Kane arrived back in Germany on Tuesday to a hero's welcome at Bayern Munich.
articles.body:
After an historic Ballon d'Or win and an emotional speech, Harry Kane arrived back in Germany on Tuesday to a hero's welcome at Bayern Munich.

"Where do I begin? That was an evening I'll never forget," Kane posted Tuesday after becoming the first English winner of the prize in 25 years and thanking his Bayern and England teammates and well-wishers. "This will live long in the memory."

- Bayern's Kompany improving 'day by day,' but no return date yet

- Kane's long road to Ballon d'Or glory ends with his crowning moment

As Kane arrived to training on Tuesday, Bayern staff formed a guard of honor as Kane walked through to loud cheers of "Harry, Harry."

Bayern are celebrating their first Ballon d'Or winner in 45 years and it's also the first for any player at a German club since 1996.

"We're all delighted with Harry Kane's performance. It's not just his goals that make him an exceptional footballer, and it's not just on the pitch that he's a special character," sporting director Christoph Freund said.

"Harry is a great guy, you very rarely come across someone like him, world-class yet so down-to-earth. Harry has taken the center-forward role to a whole new level - he's an inspiration, especially for young players. He's undoubtedly one of the greatest in football history."

Bayern have teased a "special welcome" for Kane ahead of Wednesday's German Cup second-round game against second-division Magdeburg. Danks said the England captain would be available to play Wednesday as the club continues its defense of a trophy decided last season by his hat trick in the final.

Bayern have also promised there'll be recognition of his achievement when they face arch-rival Borussia Dortmund in the Bundesliga "Klassiker" on Saturday, with Kane set to show off the trophy to Bayern supporters.

Kane is Bayern's fourth Ballon d'Or winner after German greats Franz Beckenbauer, Gerd Müller and Karl-Heinz Rummenigge, who was the last winner in 1981.

Robert Lewandowski, then at Bayern, was the runaway favorite for the prize in 2020, when a decision was taken not to award the trophy because of the COVID-19 pandemic.

The win comes at an otherwise somber time at the club, with head coach Vincent Kompany undergoing medical treatment after his sudden collapse at training last week, and midfielder Joshua Kimmich on leave after a death in the family.

"You see the extremes that life has to offer," assistant coach Aaron Danks said. "The immense joy Harry experienced yesterday and the moments we've had over the past few weeks. It's important to realize that people are what matter most."

The Associated Press contributed to this report.

articles.headline: Karabell's notebook: Murray's hot start, Adebayo's struggles, other early trends
articles.description: Eric Karabell empties out the notebook with all that he's noticing around the NBA, and what it means for fantasy.
articles.body:
I don't think many people recall that SG/PG Dejounte Murray once averaged 21.1 PPG, 8.3 RPG, 9.2 APG and 2.0 SPG for the 2021-22 San Antonio Spurs. Those numbers were outrageous!

Yeah, we knew he would not be able to replicate those numbers the following season with PG Trae Young's immense usage in Atlanta, but Murray was still very good there.

Then he went to the New Orleans Pelicans and was doing fine -- until he tore his Achilles. He played 45 games during his first two Pelicans seasons. Did fantasy managers forget the good times, or overlook them a bit?

It's early in the 2026-27 season, but Murray is back to being a modest fantasy building block, averaging 20.3 PPG, 5.0 RPG and 6.3 APG -- with 2.3 SPG and 1.3 BPG! -- for a terrible team. His usage is back and the numbers are outstanding (though the block rate cannot continue). Most fantasy managers did not see this coming.

I saw Murray's name mentioned as a potential bust, because he didn't shoot all that much when he finally debuted for his 14 appearances last season, and he was turning 30, and it's tough to thrive after a torn Achilles and, well, just stop it ...

Murray is thriving, despite the relative mess around him, and I particularly love the percentages: 49% FG and 88.9% FT is so valuable, regardless of format.

This has always been an underrated player, for fantasy purposes and otherwise. Perhaps he cannot earn his second career All-Star nod if the Pelicans never win, but fantasy managers will love him, especially those who didn't need to invest a top-60 selection on draft day to get him.

I grabbed Murray in Round 1 of a keeper league (each team kept four players), and I am glad I did.

Other observations around the NBA

My fantasy hoops preference is roto/categories formats, so I tend to love the versatile statistical options who pile on both rebounds and assists while not killing the shooting percentages. It's why I can't get enough of Hawks PF Jalen Johnson, who is averaging a near-triple double.

Chicago Bulls PG Josh Giddey won't shoot 33.3% from the field for long, right?

I see you, Orlando Magic SF/PF Franz Wagner and Brooklyn Nets PF Julius Randle.

Speaking of the Magic, now without PF/SF Paolo Banchero and PG/SG Jalen Suggs, go add PG/SG Anthony Black. He missed the first two games with an ankle sprain and then scored 18 points in 26 minutes Sunday. He won't drain five 3-pointers every game, but Black showed glimpses of fantasy stardom filling in for injured players last season. He averaged 18.2 PPG, 5.0 RPG and 5.0 APG during December/January games. The Magic must give him minutes now, and this is a good thing.

articles.headline: Knockout league pickups: Prioritize running backs while they're available
articles.description: A confluence of bye weeks and surprisingly poor performances make this the week to bid on a star running back
articles.body:
If you've been patching together the position in your Knockout league to this point, consider it a prime time to pounce for a top-shelf free agent. Between bye weeks and unexpectedly poor performances, an unusually large number of top-shelf running backs have found themselves on knocked-out teams so far in October.

The top 11 running backs in fantasy points per game have found themselves on a knocked-out team in more than 10% of leagues six times in the past three weeks alone. In fact, Derrick Henry, ninth in total points (122.7) and 11th in points per game (17.5), has been on the list in back-to-back weeks, after scoring fewer than 10 points in Weeks 6 (5.0) and 7 (5.9).  The last time he had scored in single digits was Week 5 of last season.

The bye weeks have had a lot to do with this availability trend. In Week 5, it was RB2 (going by points per game) Kenneth Walker III and RB9 Chuba Hubbard. In Week 6, RB1 Jahmyr Gibbs took his turn. This past week, RB7 James Cook III had his bye. Hubbard was the only one of them whose knocked-out rate finished beneath 10% in that week (he was on eliminated teams in 8.5% of leagues), which you can attribute to the fact that you didn't spend a one of your top two picks on him.

It doesn't get any easier on the availability front: RB4 Christian McCaffrey's bye week is up next, and RB3 Bijan Robinson's arrives three weeks after that, during Bye-Maggeddon.

In a season where having an elite running back has proven particularly advantageous, now is the time to open up your FAB wallet and strengthen the position, assuming, of course, you're not already the lucky manager of one of the aforementioned seven players. Getting one with his bye in the rearview is even more beneficial.

This is the first time all season that three of these top 11 positional scorers have found themselves available via free agency in at least 10% of Knockout leagues, and two of them (Cook and Walker) fit the rearview-bye description. Even McCaffrey's managers should consider spending big on a top-shelf running back, bridging the San Francisco 49ers star's bye week, then providing an elite one-two punch for the season's final nine weeks. Remember, piecing together quarterback and wide receiver via the matchups route becomes easier with each passing week as your league size shrinks.  There's only so many elite running backs.

The 20 most-knocked-out players exiting Week 7

Note that FAB recommendations are in three tiers: "% OF FAB TO BID (ENFORCE)" is a low-end recommendation, if you don't necessarily need the player but don't want him gifted to the competition. "% OF FAB TO BID (MEDIAN)" is the recommended bid for a team with average needs at that position. "% OF FAB TO BID (AGGRESSIVE)" is advised for teams thin at that specific spot.

My favorite pickup of the week

Kenneth Walker III, RB, Kansas City Chiefs (10.3% Knocked out, 15th overall, RB5): Neither he nor his Chiefs had an especially good Week 7, as he scored a season-low 9.7 fan

articles.headline: Transfer rumors, news: Dortmund's Nmecha among Liverpool's midfield targets
articles.description: Several midfielders across Europe are reportedly linked with a move to Liverpool. Transfer Talk has the latest.
articles.body:
Borussia Dortmund midfielder Felix Nmecha is one of several midfielders linked with a move to Liverpool, while Reds midfielder Alexis Mac Allister has admirers at Real Madrid. Join us for the latest transfer news and rumors from around the globe.

Transfers home page | Men's summer grades | Women's grades

Trending rumors

- Liverpool hold Borussia Dortmund midfielder Felix Nmecha in "high regard", Sky Germany has revealed. While the 26-year-old is not currently a priority target, that could change in the future as the Reds target reinforcements in his position. AS Monaco's Lamine Camara and AFC Bournemouth's Alex Scott are both on Liverpool's central midfielder shortlist, players who have also been linked with the likes of Chelsea and Manchester United in recent months. Nmecha, meanwhile, is under contract at Dortmund until June 2030, having joined the club in 2023 from Wolfsburg.

- Real Madrid could make a move for Liverpool midfielder Alexis Mac Allister in a future transfer window, reports Sky Germany. José Mourinho is an advocate of signing the 27-year-old, particularly admiring his physical presence and strength in challenges. The Argentine international is contracted at Anfield until 2028, with no concrete plans currently in place to extend. Madrid are monitoring his situation, although Liverpool would be expected to resist any approach for a key player.

- Arsenal are interested in Monza striker Gustavo Varela, La Gazzetta dello Sport reports. The 21-year-old Portuguese forward has scored seven goals in eight Serie A matches this season, attracting interest from Napoli and former club Benfica. Napoli could make their move in January to beat the competition, while Benfica retain the right to match future offers and are entitled to 20% of the profit from his next transfer.

- Manchester United remain interested in Newcastle United left back Lewis Hall, who could cost upwards of £70 million, Football Insider reports. The 22-year-old recently extended his contract until 2031, but United could revive their pursuit next summer, with Newcastle set to reject any January departure. Hall is believed to be happy at St James' Park, although he has not ruled out a future move to Old Trafford.

- Bayern Munich are closely monitoring Borussia Mönchengladbach's Wael Mohya, according to Sky Germany. Borussia Dortmund, RB Leipzig, Bayer Leverkusen and leading clubs abroad are also interested in the 17-year-old, although a winter transfer is considered unlikely at this stage. Gladbach want to extend his contract beyond 2028 as soon as possible, with a release clause included. However, Mohya staying beyond next summer is only considered conceivable if the club avoid relegation.

articles.headline: Wayne Rooney's son, Kai scores, 4 goals for Man United under-18s vs. Burnley
articles.description: Kai Rooney scored four goals as Manchester United's Under-18s thrashed Burnley 6-0 on Tuesday.
articles.headlineJa: ウェイン・ルーニーの息子カイ、バーンリー戦でマンU U-18として4ゴールを記録
articles.descriptionJa: 火曜日に行われたマンチェスター・ユナイテッドU-18のバーンリー戦において、6-0の圧勝を収める中、カイ・ルーニーが4ゴールを挙げた。
articles.body:
Kai Rooney scored four goals as Manchester United's under-18s thrashed Burnley 6-0 on Tuesday.

Kai, son of United's all-time leading goalscorer Wayne, stole the show as Darren Fletcher's side cruised to a convincing victory in the Under-18 Premier League North.

The 16-year-old opened the scoring after 22 minutes, as he knocked home the rebound after Jaume Camacho's header struck the post.

The teenager doubled his tally from the penalty spot shortly after halftime, having been brought down by Burnley captain Dylan Morison.

He completed his hat trick in the 63rd minute, heading home Jay McEvoy's corner, before adding a fourth just three minutes later with a powerful finish from inside the box.

Camacho and substitute Noah Ajayi added late goals to complete the rout, sending United second in the table with six wins from their opening eight league games.

Rooney is looking to follow in the footsteps of his father, who became of the best players in the world at United and a bona fide club legend.

- Wayne Rooney blasts Man United players amid growing crisis

- Michael Carrick to lead Man United vs. Chelsea amid uncertain future - sources

- Gary Neville: 'Really surprised' but 'happy' Michael Carrick set to continue as Man United boss

The eldest of Wayne and Coleen Rooney's four sons, he joined United's academy in December 2020, aged 11, and this season made his first appearance at the under-21 level.

A number of United under-18s have recently earned senior debuts, including Chido Obi, Harry Amass and Shea Lacey.

articles.headline: Bayern Munich's Vincent Kompany improving 'day by day,' but no return date yet
articles.description: Bayern Munich assistant coach Aaron Danks said head coach Vincent Kompany is in good spirits and improving "day by day" after being hospitalized last week.
articles.headlineJa: バイエルン・ミュンヘンのヴィンセント・コンパニー、容体は「日ごとに改善」も復帰時期は未定
articles.descriptionJa: バイエルン・ミュンヘンのアーロン・ダンクス助監督は、先週入院したヴィンセント・コンパニー監督について、気分は良く「日ごとに」改善していると述べた。
articles.body:
Bayern Munich assistant coach Aaron Danks said head coach Vincent Kompany is in good spirits and improving "day by day" after being hospitalized last week.

Kompany collapsed at the club's training ground on Friday and missed Sunday's 3-1 win away at Freiburg.

- Kane's long road to Ballon d'Or glory ends with his crowning moment

Sporting director Max Eberl said on Friday that it would be "weeks, not days" before the Belgian coach was able to return to work, but, speaking at a news conference ahead of Wednesday's German Cup clash with Magdeburg, Danks said he had visited Kompany and he was doing well.

"I popped in to see Vincent briefly yesterday," he said. "He's in good spirits. It looks as though things are improving day by day. There's no definitive prognosis.

"He's very calm and is being given plenty of time to recover. We had some good chats, but they had nothing to do with football or tactics. He asked how we were getting on."

Harry Kane could make his first appearance since being crowned Ballon d'Or winner when Bayern play second-tier Magdeburg in the second round of the cup.

"He [Kompany] actually phoned me [on Monday] morning, phoned me bright and early at 9 a.m. and I was just out of bed thankfully," Kane said after the ceremony in London on Monday.

"He just wanted to wish me all the best and good luck. I asked him how he was doing. He said he feels good and feels like he is on the mend, so I know he is the type of character that just wants to be back with the team already, out on the training field, out on the bench with us but it's important that he rests.

"He's been going through a bit of a tough time with his health recently. The staff can cover it when he's not there, but looking forward to going back to Munich to see him, to see all the staff, all my teammates.

"I have spoken about how this is theirs as much as ours so to celebrate with them a little bit, it will be special."

Kane was asked whether he saw his long-term future at the Allianz Arena or if he would consider returning to England to try and challenge Alan Shearer's 260-goal Premier League record.

"Bayern is such a great club, we have an amazing team, a great coach, so right now that is where my focus is and I am extremely happy to be winning awards like this," Kane said.

"It shows why I made the move in the first place. Of course there is always ambition, always dreams and new things.

"I've learnt you don't have much of a say, you just have to go with the flow and see where it takes you."

PA contributed to this report.

articles.headline: Lens fans banned from Liverpool match for throwing flares vs. Brugge
articles.description: Fans of Ligue 1 club Lens were banned from buying tickets for a Champions League game at Liverpool by a UEFA disciplinary ruling Tuesday.
articles.body:
NYON, Switzerland -- Fans of Ligue 1 club Lens were banned from buying tickets for a Champions League game at Liverpool by a UEFA disciplinary ruling on Tuesday.

Lens fans lit dozens of flares and threw some toward rival supporters and the field, forcing the team's Champions League game at Club Brugge last week to be stopped briefly. Lens lost 3-0.

The club already were on probation by UEFA for fans lighting flares and fireworks at a previous Champions League game at Slavia Prague in September.

UEFA said its appeals judges imposed a ban on Lens selling tickets to fans for two Champions League away games.

The sanction will be served when Lens play at Leipzig on Nov. 24 and at Liverpool at Anfield on Jan. 27. A third game ban is deferred for a two-year probationary period.

UEFA said Lens were fined €80,000 ($89,000) for charges of "lighting and throwing of pyrotechnics as well as for acts of damage."
